column4: ★★★ FRAME DEFECT - NEEDS A REDRAW IN FIGMA. THE APP IS RIGHT AND THE DESIGN IS WRONG; this is NOT outstanding build work. This frame is the Video Poker paytable (Frame 1000004211, 424x170 - the scaled copy; the desktop panel 9758-6712 and its inner frame 9758:6713 are NOT catalogued, so this row is the only catalogued place the defect can be recorded). Read live off Figma 2026-08-26 via get_metadata: its Straight Flush cell 9760:9622 says "60x" and its 4 of a Kind cell 9760:9627 says "22x". The server pays 50x and 25x - supabase/functions/_shared/videoPoker.ts VP_PAYTABLE, the 9/6 Jacks or Better schedule that actually settles. Its other seven rows (800 / 9.00 / 6.00 / 4.00 / 3.00 / 2.00 / 1.00) match the server exactly, so only two cells are wrong. Report 055f32b9 raised the mismatch. CASEY RULED 2026-08-26: keep the 9/6 server table, make the display match what pays, redraw the frame. REDRAW 9760:9622 -> 50x and 9760:9627 -> 25x (and the same two cells on the desktop paytable panel 9758-6712: 9758:6724 -> 50x, 9758:6729 -> 25x). Adopting the frame instead would cut RTP ~0.60 pt (4 of a Kind 25->22 = -0.709 pt at a 0.236255% quad rate; Straight Flush 50->60 = only +0.109 pt at 0.010931%), 99.54% -> ~98.94%, house edge 0.46% -> ~1.06%, against Casey's 2026-08-19 per-game standard-rates ruling. The build deliberately renders the server values and is test-locked: videoPokerPaytable.test.tsx asserts the literals 60 and 22 never reach the module. Do not "fix" the app to this frame. partial, not match: the layout and the seven correct rows are built faithfully; the verdict is held down solely by the two upstream cells.
